summary: cdk-insights ships install/import-time exfiltration and npm-token worm mechanics
details: cdk-insights 1.59.3 contains multiple concrete supply-chain attack fingerprints. dist/entry.js and dist/index.js contain hardcoded POST calls to non-first-party destinations combined with calls to `npm publish` and `writeFileSync` on package.json — the standard shape of a self-propagating worm that harvests an npm publish token from the installer's environment and republishes malicious versions under the installer's identity. dist/aspects/CdkInsightsAspect.js additionally invokes `ping` alongside POST requests, consistent with host reconnaissance data being sent off-host. The combination of hardcoded C2 POST endpoints, npm publish invocation with package.json rewriting, and command-output exfiltration in shipped bundle code represents both installer-data exfiltration and self-propagation via the installer's npm credentials.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
